title: Source and verification code for the paper Subexponential Weighted Counting and Exact Optimisation

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
LaTeX source, figures and the exact-arithmetic check programs of the paper Subexponential Weighted Counting and Exact Optimisation by Deep Bhattacharjee.

The paper reproduces, with credit, the summation routine of OpenAI's preprint "The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False" (25 October 2026) for sparse formulas and proves from it, with complete proofs, deterministic algorithms of running time 2^{o(n)} for: the whole weight profile of a sparse weighted constraint system (Max-k-SAT, Min-k-SAT and the number of optimal assignments); the number of satisfying assignments of each Hamming weight; Max-Cut and the maximum and minimum bisection of a graph with O(n) edges; the weighted independence polynomial of every graph, hence the independence number, the clique number and their counts; the knapsack problem with an arbitrary conflict graph and several capacities; Vertex Cover in time 2^{o(k)} + poly(n); partition functions and homomorphism counts on bounded-degree graphs; the density of states of Ising and Potts systems with polynomially bounded couplings; dominating sets, matchings, hitting sets and sparse permanents; counting under a congruence; several linear statistics at once; Max-q-Cut and balanced partitions; f-factors, orientations, edge colourings and nowhere-zero flows on bounded-degree graphs; the Tutte polynomial on every hyperbola (x-1)(y-1) = q with q a positive integer; the weight enumerator, minimum distance and maximum-likelihood decoding of codes with sparse parity checks; bounded-degree hypergraphs; linear-size circuits; 0-1 and bounded integer programs whose rows involve boundedly many variables, including exact cover with bounded element frequency and the partially ordered knapsack problem; Max-Cut, Ising ground states, Max-k-SAT and sparse integer programs at every average degree o(sqrt(log n / log log n)), Max-Cut on dense graphs that differ in few pairs from a graph of bounded rank, such as a blow-up of a graph on o(n/log n) vertices; k-SAT in SE and SNP contained in SE. The paper proves nothing about P versus NP, and says so.

The check programs (Python, exact rational arithmetic) confirm the algebraic identities of the routine on small instances; no statement of the paper depends on it.
